title: Preserve exact located target at the canvas center

scope.subject: Make a completed YEIS Locate own a bounded center-click affinity without replacing the existing picker priority or camera authority

research_summary: The existing pinned YEIS CameraController correctly centers Locate targets, but the Personal Universe adapter then resolves a center click through independent projected overlays before the native landmark picker. Runtime probing after locating Orion Nebula showed unrelated Personal Signal, Hero and observed-host overlays can all project within the generic desktop pick radius near the exact center, so shrinking individual hitboxes only moves the false winner. Reuse the existing YEIS Locate request/settlement state and shared destination executor: after a Locate completes, retain the exact located destination identity as a bounded center-click affinity. A click within the normal center hit radius opens that located destination; clicks away from center continue through the existing Personal Signal -> Hero -> observed -> landmark -> galaxy -> star picker order. Clear the affinity on a new navigation request or manual camera takeover so it cannot become a stale second navigation authority.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS already owns CameraController centering/autopilot and the imperative Input click path; the fix should preserve that authority and adapt only post-Locate click resolution.
Three.js projection remains the existing screen-space primitive for overlay hit testing, but projection alone cannot encode the semantic fact that a user deliberately centered a Locate target.

camera-controls supplies generic smooth Three.js camera controls but does not own YEIS reference frames, Locate identity, or the existing native picker; introducing it would create competing camera/navigation authority.

search_ladder.conclusion: A separate spatial-navigation or annotation product would duplicate the existing YEIS universe, destination model and canvas picker for a single post-Locate interaction gap.

React Three Fiber already hosts the canvas and pointer surface; replacing the imperative YEIS picker with a second R3F interaction graph solely for post-Locate center clicks would duplicate native renderer ownership.
Pinned YEIS CameraController/Input plus the existing Personal Universe navigation request state already contain the exact target and settlement boundary needed for center affinity.

Three.js Vector3 projection is retained for normal overlay picking, while camera-controls is rejected because it would add a competing camera authority rather than solve semantic post-Locate identity.

candidates.name: Existing YEIS Locate settlement plus destination identity
candidates.source: Pinned MIT YEIS CameraController/Input adapted through the existing navigation request
candidates.reason: It already owns the exact Locate target, camera settlement and native input path; retaining that identity for one bounded center click closes the ambiguity without another camera or picker system.

candidates.name: Rebuild picking as React Three Fiber pointer events
candidates.reason: R3F is already the host, but rebuilding imperative YEIS sky/landmark picking as a second interaction graph is larger than the gap and risks diverging from pinned native Input semantics.

candidates.name: camera-controls replacement camera path
candidates.reason: Generic lookAt/fit transitions do not preserve YEIS hierarchical reference frames or native destination identity and would create a second camera authority.

coverage_matrix.capability: Preserve exact Locate target identity through camera settlement
coverage_matrix.decision: Reuse the existing YEIS navigation request and settlement state rather than infer the target again from overlapping projected markers.

coverage_matrix.capability: Keep existing picker priority everywhere away from the deliberate located center
coverage_matrix.decision: Apply affinity only inside the normal center hit radius and otherwise preserve the existing picker unchanged.

coverage_matrix.capability: Avoid stale affinity after subsequent navigation or manual camera control
coverage_matrix.decision: Clear the retained located target when a new navigation request starts and when native input takes over the camera.

decision.rationale: Reuse the pinned YEIS Locate/camera/input subsystem and add only a bounded semantic adapter at the existing click dispatcher. This fixes the overlap class globally while preserving the native picker, Personal Signal priority and single camera authority.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: A framework-level picker rebuild can cover pointer input but duplicates the already-hosted native YEIS imperative scene and does not inherently know which destination the user intentionally located.

decision.fallback: If center affinity proves too sticky in manual validation, clear it on any pointer drag/wheel/key camera input and retain it only until the first post-Locate click.
